summary: This Wikipedia-derived note is a broad overview of Nigeria, covering its satellites (NigComSat-1 and NigeriaSat-2), religious demographics across surveys, Boko Haram violence, the oil sector, politics and the transition to democracy in 1999, education, population and census data, the 419 advance-fee scams, geography, football, languages, economy, and its history of trade and the slave trade. It also notes that Nigeria is Africa's most populous country and largest economy. The content is a compilation of multiple sections of the Nigeria article rather than a single focused topic.
one_line: Wikipedia overview of Nigeria covering its satellites, religion, politics, economy, education, geography, history and culture.
key_facts: NigComSat-1 was launched on 13 May 2007 aboard a Chinese Long March 3B rocket from the Xichang Satellite Launch Centre in China.
NigComSat-1 failed in orbit on 11 November 2008 after running out of power because of an anomaly in its solar array.
NigeriaSat-2 was built by Surrey Space Technology Limited, a United Kingdom-based company, at a cost of over £35 million.
Boko Haram has carried out sectarian violence in North East Nigeria since 2002, and President Goodluck Jonathan claimed in May 2014 that attacks had left at least 12,000 people dead.
The Nembe Creek Oil field in the Niger Delta was discovered in 1973.
In 2003 the Nigerian Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) was created to combat organised financial crime, including 419 advance fee fraud.
Nigeria regained democracy in 1999 when it elected Olusegun Obasanjo, the former military head of state, as President, ending almost 33 years of military rule.
The 2006 census gave a population of 140,003,542.
The 2010 Pew Research Center report stated that 49.3 percent of Nigeria's population was Christian and 48.8 percent was Muslim.
Nigeria's literacy rate is 68%, with men at 75.7% and women at 60.6%.
With 186 million inhabitants, Nigeria is the most populous country in Africa and the seventh most populous country in the world.
As of 2015, Nigeria is the world's 20th largest economy and overtook South Africa to become Africa's largest economy in 2014.
Nwankwo Kanu, a two-time African Footballer of the Year, won the European Champions League with Ajax Amsterdam.
Nigeria is a founding member of the Commonwealth of Nations, the African Union, OPEC, and the United Nations.
Nigeria is divided roughly in half between Christians, who live mostly in the south, and Muslims, who live mostly in the north.
